summary: Updates RFC 9171 to clarify that Bundle Protocol Version 7 agents are expected to use the IANA Bundle Administrative Record Types registry to identify and document administrative record types. It also designates code points for private and experimental use.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9713 clarifies how Bundle Protocol Version 7 agents identify administrative record types. It updates the IANA registry by version and reserves code points for experimental and private use.

subtitle: Clarifies registry use and reserves Bundle Protocol Version 7 code points.

tldr.problem: The Bundle Protocol Version 7 specification named an administrative record registry but did not clearly map entries to protocol versions or distinguish reserved values from unassigned ranges.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC updates the registry with a Bundle Protocol Version column, directs BPv7 agents to use it, and reserves code points for experimental and private use.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9713 updates RFC 9171 with clearer administrative record identification and code point reservations.

today: RFC 9713 is a Proposed Standard from January 2025 and updates RFC 9171.

sections.title: Why the Registry Needed an Update
sections.content:
RFC 7116 established an IANA registry for administrative record type code points used with Bundle Protocol Version 6 (BPv6). RFC 9171 identified that registry for BPv7 but did not make clear which entries applied to which protocol versions. It also did not distinguish code point reservations from unassigned ranges.

RFC 9713 updates BPv7 to use the existing registry and reserves high-valued code points for private and experimental use. It does not specify how BPv6 and BPv7 interoperate when they use the same code point.
sections.plainLanguage: The old registry did not clearly show which protocol version could use each record type. This update makes version use explicit and sets aside ranges for experiments and private use.

sections.title: Registry Entries and Reserved Ranges
sections.content:
The registry gains a Bundle Protocol Version column. A BPv7 administrative element determines usable record type codes from entries marked with version 7. The zero value is reserved for consistency with BPv6.

For BPv7, values 64384-64511 are reserved for Experimental Use, and 64512-65535 are reserved for Private Use. The RFC also adds a code point that had been allocated in the cited CCSDS specification but was not yet in the IANA registry.
sections.plainLanguage: Check the new version column to see which record types BPv7 can use. Values 64384 through 64511 are for experiments, and 64512 through 65535 are for private use.

sections.title: Handling Unknown Administrative Records
sections.content:
If an administrative element receives an administrative record type it cannot process, or a malformed application data unit, it SHALL ignore that record. Processing the record does not change whether the enclosing bundle was delivered to the administrative element.

Other bundle protocol processing for the enclosing bundle, such as status reports, is also unaffected by processing the administrative record.
sections.plainLanguage: If a BPv7 element cannot process an administrative record, it must ignore that record. This does not undo delivery of the bundle that carried it.
